name: Tessera Neural Assault System TNAS-1 'Puppeteer'
description:
The TNAS-1 Puppeteer represents Tessera's most aggressive integration of neural technology with small arms. The weapon cannot be fired by trigger pull — it has no trigger. The Puppeteer fires exclusively through BCI neural command, with the operator's intent translated into firing decisions by an onboard neural interpretation engine. Think 'fire' and it fires. Think 'burst' and it fires three rounds. Think 'suppress' and it dumps a magazine at the designated area.

The rifle chambers 5.8mm caseless and features a free-floating barrel in a fully sealed receiver that eliminates environmental ingress. Without a trigger mechanism, trigger guard, or manual safety, the weapon's exterior is a smooth polymer shell with no external controls beyond a physical power switch. The BCI link handles everything — fire mode selection, round counting, malfunction diagnostics, and even thermal management alerts.

The Puppeteer is the most controversial weapon in production. Advocates praise its response time — neural firing commands bypass the mechanical delay of trigger pull, reducing time-to-fire by approximately 80 milliseconds. Critics argue that a weapon fired by thought is a weapon that can be fired by intrusive thoughts, hacked neural commands, or BCI malfunction. Tessera's liability waivers for the TNAS-1 are longer than the user manual.
legality: Restricted — requires BCI certification and psychological screening
specifications:
caliber: 5.8mm caseless
effective_range: 500m
rate_of_fire: 850 rpm (cyclic, neural-commanded)
magazine_capacity: 35 rounds
weight: 3.1 kg
tactical_use: The Puppeteer offers the fastest possible engagement time for any conventional firearm. The 80ms advantage over trigger-fired weapons is marginal in isolation but decisive in close-quarters engagements where reaction time determines survival. The sealed receiver and lack of external mechanisms make the weapon virtually maintenance-free in the field. However, any disruption to the operator's BCI link renders the weapon completely inoperable — it becomes an expensive club.
cultural_context: The Puppeteer provokes visceral reactions. Neural-purists see it as the natural evolution of human-weapon integration. Traditional operators view it as a weapon that can be turned against its user by anyone with a BCI hack. The psychological screening requirement has created a secondary market for forged certification documents, and several incidents of accidental discharge by stressed operators have fueled regulatory campaigns.
story_hooks: A Puppeteer operator's BCI was hacked during an engagement, causing the weapon to fire on friendly targets. The neural intrusion was so subtle the operator believed they were shooting at enemies.
A black-market neural interface claiming to be Puppeteer-compatible is actually recording the operator's neural patterns for resale to a data broker.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, almost organic assault rifle with no visible mechanical protrusions. The Puppeteer presents as a smooth, integrated form factor — more like a precision instrument than traditional small arms. Its silhouette tapers toward the muzzle with subtle ergonomic curves that suggest neural-responsive design rather than mechanical function.
physical_description.dimensions: 680mm overall length, 55mm width at receiver, 110mm height with optics rail. Barrel length: 420mm. Magazine well: 35-round capacity requiring deep grip.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light at 3.1kg — feels almost weightless in trained hands, yet the weight distribution is front-heavy due to sealed receiver components and neural interpretation engine housing behind the receiver. Balanced but suggests hidden density.
physical_description.primary_material: Advanced polymer composite (graphene-reinforced bio-polymer) with embedded circuitry layers. Fully sealed aluminum alloy receiver housing neural interpretation engine and power distribution.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal polymer with subtle iridescent shift under angled light — evidence of embedded neural response substrate. Internal geometry visible through semi-translucent polymer panels at receiver sides, showing circuit traces like dark capillaries.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal gray primary body with deep blue-black metallic accents at receiver endplate. Thin accent striping in cold cyan along the rail system — indicator of active neural monitoring state.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with micro-ridged surface for moisture control. The grip itself is subtly contoured and slightly warmer to touch due to embedded neural interface contact points. No traditional trigger guard — instead, a smooth thumb shelf.
distinctive_features: Complete absence of trigger, trigger guard, or manual safety — only a recessed power switch at the receiver tail
Semi-translucent polymer body panels revealing circuit patterns and component layout
Integrated BCI contact interface at grip — faint neural feedback haptics visible as micro-texture variation
Sealed muzzle brake with no visible gas ports — all exhaust managed internally
Thin status LED strip running along the top rail — cyan when active, amber when idle, red when offline
No manual charging handle — recipient only accesses magazine well and power switch
Rail-mounted optics plate with neural targeting overlay compatibility
Thermal management vents disguised as aesthetic ribbing along the receiver
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: SYNAPSE GAMING embossed discretely into the grip panel (requires angle to see). Serial plate mounted inside magazine well — not visible without magazine removal. Small Φ symbol etched above the power switch indicating Tier 4+ pricing point.
physical_description.condition_typical: Immaculate in field deployment — the sealed design eliminates visible wear patterns. Well-used units show faint micro-scratches on polymer and occasional evidence of BCI contact point burnishing on the grip. No mechanical wear, no corrosion, no fouling — maintenance is purely diagnostic through the neural link.
